rationale: Roberts is best positioned to write a narrow, institution-protective compelled-speech opinion (Hurley/Barnette/Wooley) that preserves CADA for nonexpressive goods and services while invalidating its application to bespoke message-bearing websites and likely flagging the Communication Clause. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas/Alito to press a broader compelled-speech and anti-viewpoint-discrimination rationale, and from Sotomayor (possibly joined by Jackson) to defend CADA under a FAIR-style equal-access framework and to distinguish or sever the Communication Clause issue.
